cruises.description: Day 1: Your gateway for this expedition is Ushuaia, Argentina. Located within the Tierra del Fuego archipelago, Ushuaia has a small-town feel yet boasts many shops, museums, cafés, and restaurants that you can enjoy before your voyage. Trade your land legs for sea legs, meet and greet your fellow travelers, and get acquainted with your ship. cruises.description: Day 1: With a rich Afro-Brazilian heritage, Salvador, the capital of Bahia, is a vibrant city where African and South American cultures blend. Salvador served as Brazil's first capital from 1549 to 1763, and its UNESCO World Heritage-listed historic center, Pelourinho, bursts with cobblestone streets and colorful colonial buildings. Jorge Amado, a beloved literary figure, is celebrated at his former home, now the museum Casa do Rio Vermelho. Day 2: Itacaré, a charming coastal town in southern Bahia, has miles of pristine white-sand beaches luring surfers and bodyboarders. The town's laidback charm is evident in its vibrant cobblestone streets which resonate with lively Afro-Brazilian beats…

Day 2: After a morning welcome briefing, start the day exploring the most iconic and mysterious of all things in Egypt: the Pyramids and Sphinx complex in Giza. The magnificent Pyramid of Cheops was built from over two million blocks of stone and took tens of thousands of workers twenty years to build. cruises.description: Day 1: Colón is the second-largest city in Panama, at the Caribbean entrance of the Panama Canal. Colón is today an important port, and the free trade zone created in 1953 contributed greatly to the development of the city. Colón was founded in 1850 by Americans working on the Panama railroad connecting the Atlantic and Pacific coasts through the isthmus of Panama; the city rapidly overshadowed the older Caribbean ports of Panama when the canal opened. Day 2: In the Colón District, Fort San Lorenzo faces the sea, its canons pointing towards the horizon as they used to under the Spanish Crown. cruises.description: Day 1: Arrive in Sitka, Alaska. Situated on the western coast of Baranof Island and overlooking the Pacific Ocean, Sitka is known for its Tlingit culture and remnants of its Russian heritage which date back to the 1800s. Embark this evening in time for cocktails and an introduction to the staff and crew. Today, nature is your guide as you set forth with the flexibility to take advantage of wildlife and weather conditions. You might stop at an isolated beach to take a closer look at tide pools, beachcomb, and hike stunning forest trails. Keep an eye out for old bear tracks…

Just like the legendary explorers, now it is your turn to set a course for the High Arctic. If you arrive early in Tromsø, take the opportunity to ride the Fjellheisen cable car for wide views over this city, located some 200 miles north of the Arctic Circle. Stroll past the modernist Arctic Cathedral, duck into cozy cafés glowing with festive lights, and keep one eye on the water: whales are sometimes spotted offshore. cruises.description: Day 1: The capital of the Solomon Islands, Honiara sits on the northeastern coast of Guadalcanal at the mouth of the Matanikau River. cruises.description: Day 1: Your expedition begins in Reykjavík, a city that rewards a longer look. Stroll Laugavegur for independent shops and coffee, take in the striking Hallgrímskirkja church, or lose an afternoon in the city's galleries and museums. If you can, consider booking a pre-voyage program to explore the Blue Lagoon, Þingvellir. National Park, and the Langjökull glacier. From here, it's time to board MS Fridtjof Nansen and get ready for departure. Day 2: Snæfellsnes is a peninsula of dramatic coastlines, volcanic peaks, lava fields, black-sand beaches, and traditional fishing villages, all set beneath the glacier-capped Snæfellsjökull volcano. It inspired Jules Verne's book, Journey to the Centre…

cruises.description: Day 1: Arrive in Papeete, the vibrant capital of French Polynesia. Transfer from the airport to the meetup hotel for breakfast before embarking the ship. Day 2: An uplifted coral atoll, the island of Makatea is among the Pacific's most unusual and geologically fascinating landforms. Raised dramatically from the sea by tectonic forces, Makatea stands in striking contrast to the region's low-lying atolls, with towering limestone cliffs and rugged elevated terrain. So distinctive is this rare formation that the island's name has become the term used for uplifted coral atolls around the world. cruises.description: Day 1: After an early-morning flight into Sitka from Vancouver, you'll arrive in a city set in the heart of Tongass National Forest. This has been the ancestral homeland of the Łingít people for 10,000 years. Russian explorers settled here at the turn of the 19th century, and Russia, weakened by the Crimean War, sold the territory to the United States in 1867. Today, those layers of history remain visible: at the Russian Orthodox Cathedral and Russian Bishop's House, and in the Łingít and Haida totem poles at Sitka National Historical Park. cruises.description: Day 1: Arrive in Papeete, the vibrant capital of French Polynesia. Transfer from the airport to the meetup hotel for breakfast before embarking the ship. Day 2: An uplifted coral atoll, the island of Makatea is among the Pacific's most unusual and geologically fascinating landforms. Raised dramatically from the sea by tectonic forces, Makatea stands in striking contrast to the region's low-lying atolls, with towering limestone cliffs and rugged elevated terrain. So distinctive is this rare formation that the island's name has become the term used for uplifted coral atolls around the world. cruises.description: Day 1: Today, you'll take an early flight from Seattle to Nome, Alaska, where your ship awaits for an adventure through the famed Northwest Passage and beyond. Nome is a small coastal town on the edge of the Bering Sea. Once a boomtown of the 1898 Gold Rush, it still carries traces of its frontier past in rusting dredges, old steam engines, and railway remnants. The town also drew big names, including Wyatt Earp, who opened a saloon here, and it later became the endpoint for three of Roald Amundsen's polar expeditions. That legacy of ambition and exploration sets the stage for what's to come... Once onboard, collect your expedition jacket, settle into your cabin, meet the Expedition Team,…

So distinctive is this rare formation that the island's name has become the term used for uplifted coral atolls around the world. Most international flights arrive in the late evening. Opt to arrive early for a Lima pre-voyage extension staying at the iconic Country Club Lima Hotel. The extension adds just a day to the expedition and gives you a chance to rest, relax, and see this UNESCO World Heritage-designated city. Day 2: After breakfast, fly to Iquitos in the Peruvian Amazon and continue overland to the riverside village of Nauta, where the Delfin II awaits. Settle into your cabin and gather for a welcome dinner of fine Peruvian cuisine on board. Tonight, step out…

cruises.name: Galápagos Escape
cruises.description: Day 1: Arrive in Quito, Ecuador's capital city in the Andes, where guests are met and transferred to a hotel for an overnight stay.
